title: Introduce compact 'kitchen-sink' RAG playground with TS + WASM tool shims
author: Marcus Nguyen
release_notes: Add compact multimodal RAG playground combining TypeScript UI, lightweight local indexer, and Rust->WASM tool shims for offline dev.
body:
Summary: Adds a compact, 'kitchen-sink' RAG playground that demonstrates a production-oriented developer loop: local incremental indexing, a minimal TypeScript frontend, a lightweight in-memory retriever, and Rust-compiled WASM shims that simulate external tools (search, calculator, image-metadata). This is an opinionated quickstart to help engineers prototype tool-calling agents and offline-first RAG workflows without heavy infra.

Motivation and context: Engineers repeatedly ask for a single, small-scale example that stitches several platform features together: streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs, and an offline-friendly indexer that can run in a dev container. Existing examples are either single-focus (only tool-calling or only indexing) or require cloud services. This PR provides a local-first bundle that mirrors how customers compose these building blocks in Redwood deployments and ties into the docs site quickstart. Linked Linear tickets: ENG-9401 (playground blueprint), PM-2103 (docs quickstart).

What this PR contains (high level):
- A compact TypeScript playground UI (playground/ts-app) with a minimal chat panel, streaming stub, and structured output validator. The UI runs a dev server and includes seeded prompts and step-by-step onboarding.
- A local incremental indexer (playground/indexer) that produces small L2 JSON indexes optimized for the included examples; supports incremental adds and simple vector similarity via cosine using precomputed embeddings (mocked in dev mode).
- Rust tool shims compiled to WASM (playground/tools/wasm): calculator, web-search-stub, and image-metadata-extractor. The shims expose deterministic interfaces for tool-calling tests and can run in Node and browser via WASM-bindgen.
- Example agent harness (playground/agent) that wires Redwood TS SDK calls to the UI, demonstrates function calling, structured output parsing, and a replayable session recorder for e2e developer assertions.
- Docs site update (docs/quickstarts/rag-kitchen-sink.md) with stepwise instructions, architecture diagram, and troubleshooting tips.

Commits:
- 1f3b9c2: initial playground scaffold: TS app + indexer + README + basic wiring
- c9d4b11: add Rust tool shims, wasm build scripts, and CI wasm test shim
- 3a7f2aa: agent harness + recorder, structured-output validator, replay fixtures
- e1b0f07: docs quickstart and troubleshooting, example prompts, license header fixes

Files touched (high level):
- playground/ts-app/src/* (UI and streaming client)
- playground/indexer/* (indexer CLI and sample dataset)
- playground/tools/wasm/* (Rust crates, build.rs, wasm-bindgen glue)
- playground/agent/* (TS harness, replay fixtures)
- docs/quickstarts/rag-kitchen-sink.md
- scripts/ci-wasm-test.sh, .github/workflows/playground-ci.yml (small CI workflow)

Testing and CI:
- Added a lightweight GitHub Actions workflow that runs: cargo test (wasm build check), node unit tests for the TS harness, and a smoke e2e that runs the replay harness in headless mode. The initial CI run had a flaky wasm bindgen network step; I added a retry and local artifact caching. After the retry the full CI passed on this branch. ci_status shows pass.

Review notes and decisions:
- Security: Rust WASM shims are intentionally deterministic and sandboxed; they do not perform outbound network calls in dev mode (web-search-stub returns seeded fixtures). This keeps the quickstart safe for offline or air-gapped demos.
- Mocking vs real embeddings: To make the quickstart fast and deterministic, embeddings are mocked with seeded vectors by default but the indexer includes an optional flag to call a real embedding provider for advanced users. This is documented.
- Size: The goal was to keep the bundle small (< 15MB compressed when built) so it can run in a devcontainer. Binary artifacts are not checked in; CI builds wasm artifacts on demand.

Review conversation (high level timeline):
- Amina Desai (reviewer): "Love the end-to-end story. Two asks: (1) add a short smoke test that validates a tool call chain in the replay harness, (2) clarify offline security assumptions in the README."
- Marcus Nguyen (author): "Added smoke test (playground/agent/tests/replay-smoke.spec.ts) and expanded README to call out offline defaults and embed flag. PTAL."
- Rory Patel (reviewer): "WASM packaging looks good; one nit on CI: use actions/cache for cargo registry to speed subsequent runs."
- Marcus Nguyen: "Switched CI to use actions/cache and added a short note in docs about caching strategy for local dev."
- Elena Ortiz (approver): "Docs are clear and the example is compact enough for the quickstarts section. Approved."

Edge cases and known limitations:
- The web-search-stub intentionally returns limited results; it is not intended as a production search integration. Customers should wire a real search tool for high-fidelity retrieval.
- The mocked embeddings trade fidelity for deterministic tests. The indexer supports a flag (--real-embed) to opt into real embeddings which requires API keys (described in docs).
- WASM performance in the browser is intentionally unoptimized; the example targets developer ergonomics, not production latency.

Merge and rollout:
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-02 by Amina Desai.
- Docs site quickstart added to the next docs release; docs/quickstarts/rag-kitchen-sink.md includes migration notes for existing quickstarts.

How to try locally (short):
1) git clone && cd playground/ts-app
2) ./scripts/dev-setup.sh (installs npm, builds wasm shims)
3) npm run dev (open http://localhost:5173)
4) run the replay harness: node playground/agent/replay.js --fixture=fixtures/basic-flow.json

If anything breaks: see docs/quickstarts/rag-kitchen-sink.md troubleshooting. Special thanks to Amina, Rory, and Elena for the reviews.

Changelog blurb (for release notes): Adds a compact local-first RAG playground combining TypeScript UI, an incremental indexer, and Rust->WASM tool shims to accelerate prototyping of tool-calling agents and replayable developer tests.
